transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-08-19
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE); Jordan Li (Redwood SE); Priya Shah (Solaris Head of Platform); Liam O'Connor (Solaris InfoSec); Ana Gomez (Solaris Cloud Eng); Markus Berg (CTO)

Summary:
Quick security posture intake to determine whether Solaris can go Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem). Primary concerns: SOC 2/ISO alignment, SSO/SAML integration, RBAC + least privilege, audit logs and retention, encryption/KMS and key custody, and data residency/retention for payments and PII. Customer also wants an initial cost/latency tradeoff conversation and a POC plan for an on-prem evaluation.

Topics:
- Compliance posture (SOC 2 type II, ISO 27001)
- Authentication (SAML/SSO, SCIM, SSO IdPs)
- KMS options (customer-managed keys vs Redwood-managed)
- Audit logging, retention, and log export
- Deployment modes and network requirements (VPC peering, private link, airgapped POC)
- Next steps and POC scheduling

Action items above (see metadata).

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. I'm Maya, I'm the AE on this, and Jordan is our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:12] Priya (Solaris): Hi Maya, hey Jordan. Doing well. We wanted to get into the security nitty gritty — we have to map this to our SOC 2, ISO work and get legal comfortable.
[00:20] Jordan (Redwood): Great. Quick agenda — run through compliance requirements, auth and keys, logging, deployment options, then agree next steps. Sound good?
[00:28] Markus (CTO): Yep. We have a strict retention policy for payment tokens and some PII, so that will drive whether we can use hosted.
[00:37] Liam (InfoSec): And we need customer-controlled keys for anything that touches cardholder data. We prefer KMS in our cloud account.
[00:45] Maya: Understood. We support Redwood Hosted where keys are Redwood-managed, Dedicated which is reserved capacity but still within Redwood cloud, and Private which can be VPC-based or full on-prem. Jordan, want to unpack KMS options?
[00:58] Jordan: Sure. For Hosted we can do encrypted volumes and server-side encryption, but by default the KMS is ours. For Dedicated we offer an option to bring your own key via cross-account CMKs or a KMS proxy; for Private we support direct integration with your KMS or HSM. There's some nuance around key rotation and auditability.
[01:18] Ana (Cloud Eng): When you say KMS proxy, how does network traffic flow? We can't have egress to Redwood-managed KMS for certain keys.
[01:27] Jordan: The proxy sits in the same VPC and forwards requests to your KMS using a secure tunnel; essentially the key material never leaves your account, but the service calls are proxied. There's also an HSM option for on-prem.
[01:40] Priya: For SOC 2 we need evidence of key custody and access logs. Do you produce key usage logs that we can ingest?
[01:48] Maya: Yes, we can surface key usage events in the audit log export. Jordan, details?
[01:52] Jordan: We log key operations — encrypt/decrypt, rotate, create — and you can push logs to your SIEM via our log export or S3 bucket delivery. Some customers route to Splunk/Datadog. Quick note: sometimes the export events are labeled a bit differently across providers, we can share mapping.
[02:07] Liam: Good, we need the mapping for our audit team. Also curious about RBAC. We need least-privilege roles and SSO with SAML.
[02:15] Maya: We have RBAC with roles and scopes in the Console, plus SAML SSO and SCIM for provisioning. Jordan — real-world caveats?
[02:21] Jordan: SCIM provisioning is available for user sync. With SAML you can map groups to roles. Caveat: some older IdPs require custom attribute mapping, we've had to do a bit of manual mapping for a couple customers — transcription sometimes shows 'SAML' as 'sam el' in our notes, but it's S-A-M-L.
[02:37] Ana: What about session duration and token expiry? We have strict MFA session limits.
[02:42] Jordan: You can set session timeouts at the SAML assertion level; we respect your IdP's session. Also the Console token TTLs are configurable for dedicated/private.
[02:49] Priya: Do you support IP whitelisting and conditional access?
[02:53] Maya: Yes for Dedicated and Private you get VPC controls, security groups, and private endpoints. Hosted supports allowlists and org-level controls but not VPC peering.
[03:04] Markus: Our legal will want a SOC 2 Type II report and ISO 27001 certificate. Do you have both?
[03:10] Maya: We have SOC 2 Type II and are ISO-aligned; we can share the coversheet and control mapping. We'll send the redacted report.
[03:17] Liam: Will you redact customer data from the report?
[03:19] Maya: Yes, redacted. We can provide an auditor contact if needed.
[03:24] Ana: For audit logs, how long are logs retained and can we set retention?
[03:28] Jordan: Default retention is 90 days in the Console UI, but you can export to your S3 for long-term retention. For Dedicated/Private you can set retention policies locally.
[03:36] Priya: That works but we have to retain transaction logs for 7 years for certain regs — would need a lifecycle policy.
[03:42] Jordan: Export-to-S3 with lifecycle rules is the usual pattern. If you want Redwood to manage long-term storage we have an add-on.
[03:50] Liam: Any PII scanning or data classification features?
[03:54] Maya: We don't do full DLP by default, but we can integrate with partners and run prompt-level redaction in flight. Jordan: Also you can configure prompt filters and token masking, although it's heuristic-based.
[04:08] Markus: Latency/cost — if we go Private on-prem, what's the expected perf vs Redwood Hosted?
[04:15] Jordan: On-prem will remove cross-region latency and you control the hardware — peak tokens/sec depends on your GPU. Hosted has optimized runtime and autoscaling, so for many workloads it's lower ops overhead but slightly higher egress. We'll share benchmark summaries.
[04:29] Priya: How do you handle fallbacks if a model becomes unavailable? We need guaranteed availability.
[04:33] Jordan: There are multi-model fallback policies; Dedicated has reserved capacity SLAs, Private is fully under your control. We can set up multi-region redundancy too.
[04:42] Ana: For the POC, we need a small on-prem footprint that processes masked tokens and integrates with our KMS. Can you run that without exposing any raw PII to Redwood?
[04:52] Jordan: Yes — the Private on-prem package keeps inference inside your network; we can provide an air-gapped bundle if required. There may be some operational prerequisites like a service account and outbound ports for license check, but we can negotiate.
[05:06] Priya: About encryption at rest — do you support application-level encryption on top of disk encryption?
[05:11] Jordan: You can use envelope encryption patterns and manage keys in your KMS; application-level encryption is possible with some integration work.
[05:17] Liam: For evidence collection for SOC 2, do you provide an API to pull logs for auditors?
[05:22] Maya: Yes, we provide log export APIs and time-bounded log retrieval for auditor requests.
[05:28] Markus: Any known compliance issues or previous pen test gaps we should be aware of?
[05:33] Maya: No systemic issues; we regularly remediate findings. We can share the pen test summary and remediation timeline.
[05:40] Priya: On SSO provisioning: we need group-to-role mapping and automated deprovisioning within 4 hours.
[05:47] Jordan: SCIM deprovisioning typically completes within a few minutes; 4 hours is conservative and should be attainable.
[05:54] Ana: For the audit trail, can we sign logs with our keys? We want tamper evidence for retention.
[05:59] Jordan: We can timestamp and hash logs before export; integrating with your signing infrastructure is something we can add in the Private model.
[06:08] Priya: Ok, about data residency — some customers require EU-only data. Do you support region pinning?
[06:13] Maya: Yes, region pinning is supported in Dedicated and Private. Hosted has EU regions but not hard-pinning for multi-tenant defaults; we can discuss contractual remedies for data residency.
[06:25] Liam: Our last question on regulatory: do you support HIPAA BAA?
[06:29] Maya: We have a HIPAA-ready offering and can sign a BAA for covered workloads; need to scope covered data sets.
[06:36] Markus: Great. Let's talk timeline — if we want to evaluate Private, how quickly can we get a POC?
[06:42] Jordan: Depends on hardware procurement; we can do a minimal POC with two A100-equivalent nodes in 2-3 weeks if hardware is available. If you want a cloud-hosted POC within your VPC we can spin up faster, like 3-5 days.
[06:55] Priya: Cost ballpark for on-prem POC?
[06:58] Jordan: Roughly license + support + infra. For an initial POC we'd estimate a few thousand dollars/week for nodes and a one-time setup fee; we'll provide a clearer split.
[07:08] Ana: Network requirements — what ports and egress do you need for Private?
[07:13] Jordan: Mostly egress for license checks and updates; we can provide a whitelisted set. For airgapped installs we can do offline licensing.
[07:22] Maya: Quick note — sometimes our transcripts swap technical terms, e.g., 'KV cache' might show as 'KV cash' in auto text; just flag if anything looks odd.
[07:30] Priya: Noted, thanks.
[07:33] Liam: On logs again — can we get immutability for certain buckets?
[07:37] Jordan: Yes, S3 object lock for retention immutability is an option.
[07:41] Priya: Is there an SLA for log delivery? We need assurance logs won't be delayed beyond X hours for audits.
[07:47] Jordan: For Dedicated/Private we can guarantee delivery windows; Hosted is near-real-time but we avoid hard SLAs on exports unless in an add-on.
[07:58] Markus: Any red team findings about model prompt leakage or system prompt exposures? That's a new risk for us.
[08:05] Jordan: We have prompt filtering and sandboxing; we also recommend prompt-level redaction before storage. Part of the POC can test leakage scenarios.
[08:16] Priya: Ok, let's summarize next steps.
[08:19] Maya: I'll send SOC 2 and ISO summaries and our network diagram by Friday (2026-08-21). Jordan will draft a POC plan for an on-prem minimal footprint and an alternative VPC-hosted POC, target by Sep 2. Priya, you'll confirm the list of regulated datasets and retention windows by Aug 27.
[08:34] Priya: Yes. Also please include the log export field mappings and an example audit event.
[08:39] Jordan: Will do.
[08:41] Ana: Can we get a short runbook for the SCIM + SAML mapping?
[08:44] Jordan: I'll include a mapping snippet and common IdP quirks.
[08:48] Maya: Anything else on compliance?
[08:50] Liam: We'll likely need a legal-to-legal exchange once we see the SOC report.
[08:54] Maya: Understood; we'll prepare the redacted report and a point of contact.
[08:58] Markus: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[09:01] Maya: Thanks, we'll follow up with materials.

End of transcript.

Shared artifacts referenced during call:
- SOC2-cover-and-controls.pdf (will be shared)
- Private-deployment-whitepaper.pdf (will be shared)
- POC-hardware-estimate.xlsx (Jordan to draft)
- Log-event-mapping.csv (Jordan to attach)

Meeting close:
Recap: Redwood to send compliance docs + network diagram; Jordan to scope POC; Solaris to confirm datasets and retention. Schedule follow-up for POC planning week of Sep 6 if timelines align.
